MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  January 7, 2013

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m. on Monday,
January 7, 2013, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Traina led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Savidan, Traina, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director McPherron,
Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, Administrative
Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

3.  PRESENTATIONS

Presentation by Heidi Sanborn, Executive Director of the California Product Stewardship
Council, regarding Extended Producer Responsibility.

Ms. Sanborn provided a PowerPoint presentation regarding Extended Producer Responsibility
(EPR), or Product Stewardship. In her presentation, Ms. Sanborn stated that the main goal of
EPR is to make product manufacturers responsible for the entire lifecycle of the products they
produce, including commercial waste. According to Ms. Sanborn, EPR policies strive to
internalize the environmental costs of products into their price, and to shift the economic burden
of managing products that have reached the end of their useful life from local government and
taxpayers, to product producers and consumers.

Ms. Sanborn stated that the main objective of EPR is to institute a system where manufacturers
would be required to design how the products they put on the market will be disposed of or
recycled. According to Ms. Sanborn, manufacturers are selling their products, but local
governments are paying for those products to be disposed of or recycled; Ms. Sanborn stated
  Page 1 of 4
 that local governments pay $2,500 per ton to dispose of and recycle batteries – other examples
of disposal/recycling were also provided. Ms. Sanborn stated that multiple jurisdictions,
including cities and counties, are joining in support of approaches like EPR, given their
realization of the high costs involved in recycling. However, Ms. Sanborn commented that EPR
was developed in conjunction with the private sector, and is a collaborative effort of different
organizations, including non-profits, the public sector, and the private sector.

Ms. Sanborn stressed the importance of public outreach and educating the public on how to
deal with the issues of disposal and recycling, which her organization attempts to accomplish
through workshops and by working with legislators. Finally, Ms. Sanborn asked that the City
Council adopt a resolution in support of EPR, or Product Stewardship.

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that the City has been participating in an
energy leadership partnership program, and will receive around $3,000 in rebates on energy
efficiency projects completed in City facilities.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he and Councilmember Sanchez attended a holiday
party hosted by U.S. Congresswoman Maxine Waters where they did some networking.
Councilmember Gazeley also informed those in attendance that he attended a Southern
California Association of Governments (SCAG) meeting where the Director of Housing and
Community Development made a presentation regarding the housing element.

Councilmembers Savidan and Traina wished everyone Happy New Year, and added that they
were looking forward to a productive year in 2013.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Mike Graf, Lomita resident, congratulated staff and City Council on a job well done with the
Cypress Reservoir. Mr. Graf stated that he participated in the focus group regarding water
quality and blending, and that he was very impressed as to what has been accomplished, as
well as the approach staff has taken to address reservoir issues.

George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, announced that a new
business, Western Dental, has opened in Lomita; Western Dental is located at 1920 Pacific
Coast Highway. Mr. Kivett further invited those in attendance to Western Dental's grand
opening on January 19, 2013, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Mr. Kivett also stated that U.S.
Congresswoman Maxine Waters will be attending the Chamber’s upcoming Annual Installation
of Officers and Directors. Mr. Kivett also announced that the Lomita Chamber of Commerce
selected Kaiser Permanente as their Business of the Year, and that Lomita Magnet PTA will be
awarded the Chamber's Community Service Award. Finally, Mr. Kivett asked that downtown be
decorated for the holiday season next year, and requested that the City try not to have any road
projects on the main streets during the holiday shopping season.

7. CONSENT AGENDA
  Page 2 of 4
 Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting held on
  December 17, 2012, and a Special City Council meeting held on December 3, 2012.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for Economic Development and Information Technology activities.
  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. Approval of Installation of 18 Feet of Additional Green Curb Designated for 20 Minute
  Parking Between 7 A.M. and 6 P.M., Excluding Holidays, to be Located at 25604 Narbonne
  Avenue, in front of St. Moritz Bakery. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  j. Approval of Resolution #2013-02, supporting Extended Producer Responsibility.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.  CYPRESS WATER PRODUCTION FACILITY (CWPF) - AMENDMENT NO.1 TO HAZEN
  AND SAWYER CONSULTANTS’ PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Amendment No. 1 to Hazen and Sawyer Consultant’s Professional Service Agreement and
  augmentation of the CWPF Offline Testing and laboratory budget. Presented by Public
  Works Director Damasse.

Public Works Director Damasse provided an overview of the staff report. According to Director
Damasse, on October 1, 2012, the City approved a professional services agreement with Hazen
and Sawyer Consultants to conduct offline testing at the Cypress Water Production Facility
(CWPF), in an amount not to exceed $29,892; the original scope of services focused on an
initial concept to plan an offline test using available water quality tools. Director Damasse stated
that staff met with the Water Subcommittee, a Water Focus Group, as well as other stakeholders
regarding various water quality concerns. Director Damasse stated that it became obvious that
additional testing and analysis were necessary given the comments received at previous City
Council meetings, and through public outreach meetings. Additionally, Director Damasse stated
that more extensive community outreach was necessary, and that staff had also asked Hazen
  Page 3 of 4
 and Sawyer to document their recommendations in an Operations Optimization technical
memorandum, which in turn would be used as part of the startup strategy for the City’s long-
term operation of the CWPF.

Director Damasse noted that the approved budget was established and estimated prior to
finalizing the scope of the offline testing, and based on the extra work requested by staff, Hazen
and Sawyer has requested an augmentation to their original contract in the amount of $14,484,
for labor and indirect costs associated with performing this work.

Furthermore, Director Damasse added that the original budget approved by City Council for
offline testing was $80,000, which included an estimated $10,000 in laboratory costs. According
to Director Damasse, the actual laboratory cost incurred during the offline testing, as
implemented by Hazen and Sawyer’s test plan, was $31,000 or $21,000 more than originally
estimated. Therefore, Director Damasse recommended approval of the augmentation to the
Hazen and Sawyer contract, by $14,484, as well as additions to the CWPF offline testing
laboratory budget, by $21,000. Director Damasse noted that the increased cost for Hazen and
Sawyer would be partially covered by the contingency budget, and would be paid from the
Water Capital Fund, while the lab results would be an additional expense that would also be
paid from the Water Capital Fund.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to amend the contract with Hazen and Sawyer by $14,484,
and augment the CWPF offline testing laboratory budget by $21,000. Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:48 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
